subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add true soft-steer semantics beyond current boundary steering, and should that be a new queue mode, an opt-in policy, or explicitly out of scope for now?
rationale: The requested behavior would change when active runs may be interrupted, how partial output and tool results are preserved, and which session context receives injected input; current docs intentionally define boundary steering and separate interrupt behavior.

options.title: Design an opt-in soft-steer lifecycle
options.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics, with explicit tests for streaming, tools, Codex turn/steer, fallback, and transcript state.

options.title: Keep boundary steering only
options.body: Close or narrow this feature direction and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 for remaining boundary-steering ingress bugs.

options.title: Change steer mode globally
options.body: Make existing steer more aggressive, accepting compatibility risk for users who expect current tool-boundary behavior.

recommendation.title: Design an opt-in soft-steer lifecycle
recommendation.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics, with explicit tests for streaming, tools, Codex turn/steer, fallback, and transcript state.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already handled recent maintainer review on this issue and the superseded steer PR cleanup, and the remaining question is product/runtime behavior rather than a narrow code owner fix.
